motion.reducedMotion: replace every generated or decorative animation with a still fallback
rules: Use motion only for a real perceptible wait or a completed-state transition.
Never delay completion so an animation can finish.
Pair every loading animation with written status and a static fallback.
Do not obscure training data, safety state, save state, or the primary action.

components.name: PrimaryAction
components.rule: Only one visually dominant action per decision group.

components.name: SecondaryAction
components.rule: Never compete with the primary action.

components.name: StatusChip
components.rule: Color never carries the state alone.

components.name: EvidencePanel
components.rule: Separate recorded fact, derived inference, and recommendation.

components.name: TrainingFieldGuide
components.rule: Summarize the actual recommendation and exact-source confidence without becoming a second programming authority.

components.name: QuestBubble
components.rule: Every message must be supported by completed or current session evidence.

components.name: DataInput
components.rule: Use familiar controls and never rely on placeholder text as the label.

components.name: PrimaryNavigation
components.rule: Desktop sidebar and mobile bottom navigation share the same five original destination emblems, with no icon shadow and with the written label remaining authoritative.

components.name: ForgeGlyph
components.rule: Use one reviewed GPT Images-authored family for destinations and movement families; keep other state geometry original and never imply exact exercise anatomy from a family emblem.

components.name: BodyRegionArt
components.rule: Use the anatomically clearest view, highlight only the selected region, and keep the written body-part label authoritative.

components.name: MovementFamilyArt
components.rule: Use a movement-specific reviewed scene with the defining posture and equipment; do not reuse a generic scene when it would materially misstate the movement.

components.name: ForgeLevel
components.rule: Spell out Level, keep the shadow-free badge inside the avatar footprint below the athlete, and never describe athlete ability, experience, readiness, or rank.

components.name: ProgressiveDisclosure
components.rule: Keep the current training action first and collapse notes, secondary filters, infrequent ranges, later blueprint days, the upcoming-session queue, and long Plan explanations until requested.

components.name: Modal
components.rule: Use native dialog behavior and keep the primary completion action explicit.

components.name: SoundCue
components.rule: Keep cues under 700 milliseconds, low-volume, optional, nonessential to comprehension, and independently ownable.

components.name: LoadingMoment
components.rule: Use an optimized local asset for a real wait, never create fake delay, and keep the full task usable when media fails.

components.name: TrainingBlockBlueprint
components.rule: Show the repeatable route before commitment, keep Day 1 open and later days collapsed with truthful summaries, preserve exact movement and incline choices until athlete approval, and never count estimates as completed work.

components.name: ABXAnglePicker
components.rule: Use ABX presets as touch shortcuts for incline and chest-supported adjustable-bench movements, allow any 0 to 90 degree value, and keep blank explicitly unknown.

components.name: HistoricalPerformanceEntry
components.rule: Keep past-performance entry inside the selected movement detail, preview the exact completed sets before save, preserve unknown feedback as unknown, and never imply that historical entry completed a planned workout.

components.name: SetEntryAutofill
components.rule: Copy Set 1 load, repetitions, and effort only into untouched later straight sets for the same movement; keep every field editable, require each set to be logged separately, and never alter completion, success, progression, structured technique rows, or bench-angle ladders.

components.name: RepetitionPolicyReview
states: older approved policy available for review
components.rule: Show the athlete-controlled upgrade when an older movement-placed plan can adopt route-session-v4; preview eight-plus primary Rebuild and Calibration work, ten-plus secondary work, and fifteen-repetition Freak Athlete Leg Developer work without silently rewriting the approved plan.

narrative.foreground: Fast, truthful training decisions and readable evidence.
narrative.delight: Original handheld field-guide craft, pixel scenes, selectors, badges, and earned celebrations.
narrative.boundary: No copied game IP, technique-video surface, fake progress, shame, or decorative AI filler.
